accepted.s: Under Article 368 of the Constitution, a Constitutional Amendment Bill may be introduced in Parliament by
o: A Minister or a private member in either House
Only a Minister in either House
Only a private member in the Rajya Sabha
Only a Minister in the Lok Sabha
accepted.x: A Constitutional Amendment Bill under Article 368 may be introduced in either House by a Minister or a private member.
accepted.tq: Test who is legally authorised to introduce the Bill rather than assuming it is a government-only measure.
accepted.sec: Constitutional amendment bill - joint sitting, majority

accepted.s: Which one of the following is correct regarding the introduction of a Constitutional Amendment Bill under Article 368?
o: Prior recommendation of the President is not required
Prior recommendation of the President is compulsory
The Bill can be introduced only after ratification by half the States
Prior recommendation of the Governor is required
accepted.x: A Constitutional Amendment Bill does not require the President's prior recommendation for introduction. Ratification by half the States is required only for specified federal provisions after parliamentary passage.
accepted.tq: Use the prior-sanction distinction to separate Constitutional Amendment Bills from specified financial and territorial Bills.
accepted.sec: Constitutional amendment bill - joint sitting, majority

accepted.s:
With reference to a Constitutional Amendment Bill, consider the following statements:
1. A joint sitting may be summoned if the two Houses disagree.
2. The Bill fails if either House rejects it.
3. The President is constitutionally required to give assent after the Bill is duly passed.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: There is no provision for a joint sitting in respect of a Constitutional Amendment Bill; therefore, rejection by either House causes failure. Under the 24th Amendment, 1971, the President must give assent to a duly passed Constitutional Amendment Bill.
accepted.tq: Identify the constitutional exception to the ordinary deadlock procedure and the mandatory presidential assent.
accepted.sec: Constitutional amendment bill - joint sitting, majority

accepted.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched regarding Constitutional Amendment Bills and ordinary Bills?
o: Constitutional Amendment Bill — joint sitting possible in case of deadlock
Ordinary Bill — special majority in each House separately
Constitutional Amendment Bill — federal provisions may require ratification by half the States
Ordinary Bill — President must assent in every case
accepted.x: Certain Constitutional Amendments affecting federal provisions require ratification by at least half the States. Ordinary Bills generally require a simple majority, may be subject to joint sitting, and are not covered by mandatory assent in the same manner.
accepted.tq: Compare the deadlock, majority, ratification and assent columns before selecting the correctly matched pair.
accepted.sec: Constitutional amendment bill - joint sitting, majority

accepted.s: Which of the following provisions may be amended by a simple majority of Parliament and is consequently outside the procedure of Article 368?
o: Distribution of legislative powers between the Union and the States
Election of the President of India
Creation or abolition of a State Legislative Council
accepted.x: Creation or abolition of a State Legislative Council is provided for through a simple-majority procedure outside Article 368. The other subjects involve constitutional provisions requiring the Article 368 procedure, including possible State ratification.
accepted.tq: Look for the exceptional constitutional matters that are expressly outside Article 368.
accepted.sec: Constitutional amendment bill - joint sitting, majority

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Ratification by at least half of the States is required for every Constitutional Amendment.
2. For amendments affecting specified federal provisions, State ratification is required.
3. No time limit is prescribed for such State ratification.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: State ratification is not required for every Constitutional Amendment. It is required for specified federal provisions, and no time limit is prescribed for completing that ratification.
accepted.tq: Reject the absolute word “every” and retain the federal-provision exception.
accepted.sec: Constitutional amendment bill - joint sitting, majority

accepted.s: The Constitution (131st Amendment) Bill, 2026 was negatived in the Lok Sabha because it
o: was rejected by the Rajya Sabha after a joint sitting
was returned by the President for reconsideration
failed to secure a simple majority, receiving 230 votes in favour
secured 298 votes in favour but fell short of the special majority
accepted.x: The Bill received 298 votes in favour and 230 against out of 528 members present, but this was below the special majority required for a Constitutional Amendment Bill.
accepted.tq: Match the vote figures with the constitutional majority requirement and avoid confusing simple with special majority.
accepted.sec: Constitutional amendment bill - joint sitting, majority

accepted.s: The Constitution (131st Amendment) Bill, 2026 was associated with which of the following proposals?
o: Amendment of the procedure for passing Money Bills
Creation of a new State and abolition of its Legislative Council
Fast-track women's reservation and an increase in Lok Sabha strength from 550 to 850
Simultaneous elections through insertion of Article 82A
accepted.x: The 131st Amendment Bill, 2026 concerned fast-track women's reservation and proposed increasing Lok Sabha strength from 550 to 850.
accepted.tq: Separate the two contemporary amendment proposals by their subject matter and Article reference.
accepted.sec: Universal angles

accepted.s: The Constitution (129th Amendment) Bill, 2024, which was referred to a Joint Parliamentary Committee, is associated with
o: One Nation, One Election and a proposed new Article 82A
The introduction of the annual financial statement
Fast-track women's reservation and 850 Lok Sabha seats
accepted.x: The 129th Amendment Bill, 2024 concerns simultaneous elections, or One Nation, One Election, and proposes a new Article 82A. It was referred to a Joint Parliamentary Committee.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between the two numbered contemporary Constitutional Amendment Bills by their subject and proposed Article.
accepted.sec: Universal angles

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Constitution (129th Amendment) Bill, 2024:
1. It relates to simultaneous elections.
2. It proposes a new Article 82A.
3. It had already been enacted after receiving the required two-thirds majority in both Houses.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: The Bill relates to simultaneous elections and proposes Article 82A. It remained before the Joint Parliamentary Committee and had not been enacted after securing the required majority.
accepted.tq: Use the status trap: a Bill referred to a committee must not be treated as an enacted law.
accepted.sec: Universal angles

accepted.s: Which Article of the Constitution provides for the Annual Financial Statement?
accepted.x: Article 112 provides for the Annual Financial Statement, commonly called the Union Budget.
accepted.tq: Recall the article-to-provision pair directly from the financial provisions sequence.
accepted.sec: Budget - Annual Financial Statement, Arts. 112-117, guillotine, cut motions, vote on account

accepted.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Article)
A. Article 112
B. Article 113
C. Article 114
D. Article 115

List-II (Provision)
1. Appropriation Bill
2. Supplementary, additional or excess grants
3. Annual Financial Statement
4. Procedure on estimates and demands for grants

Select the correct answer using the code given below:
accepted.x: Article 112 concerns the Annual Financial Statement, Article 113 the procedure on estimates, Article 114 the Appropriation Bill, and Article 115 supplementary, additional or excess grants.
accepted.tq: Start with the secure Article 112–Budget pair and complete the consecutive financial-Article sequence.
accepted.sec: Budget - Annual Financial Statement, Arts. 112-117, guillotine, cut motions, vote on account

accepted.s: The Union Budget is prepared by the Budget Division of the
o: Department of Expenditure, Ministry of Finance
Department of Economic Affairs, Ministry of Finance
Department of Revenue, Ministry of Finance
accepted.x: The Budget is prepared by the Budget Division in the Department of Economic Affairs, Ministry of Finance.
accepted.tq: Apply the “which department does this job?” authority-identification method.
accepted.sec: Budget - Annual Financial Statement, Arts. 112-117, guillotine, cut motions, vote on account

accepted.s: The Annual Financial Statement of the Union is laid before Parliament by the
accepted.x: The Annual Financial Statement is laid before both Houses of Parliament by the President under the constitutional financial procedure.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the authority that formally lays the statement from the authority that prepares or presents it.
accepted.sec: Budget - Annual Financial Statement, Arts. 112-117, guillotine, cut motions, vote on account

accepted.s: The first Union Budget of independent India was presented by R. K. Shanmukham Chetty on
accepted.x: R. K. Shanmukham Chetty presented the first Union Budget of independent India on 26 November 1947.
accepted.tq: Use the date-person association rather than confusing the first Budget with later Budget-calendar changes.
accepted.sec: Budget - Annual Financial Statement, Arts. 112-117, guillotine, cut motions, vote on account

accepted.s: Since 2017, the Union Budget has generally been presented on
accepted.x: From 2017 onwards, the Union Budget has generally been presented on 1 February. The Budget for 2026–27 was presented on 1 February 2026.
accepted.tq: Test the change in the Budget presentation date against the earlier historical date.
accepted.sec: Budget - Annual Financial Statement, Arts. 112-117, guillotine, cut motions, vote on account

accepted.s:
With reference to Demands for Grants, consider the following statements:
1. They are voted only by the Lok Sabha.
2. The Rajya Sabha may discuss them but cannot vote on them.
3. Charged expenditure is discussed but is not submitted to vote.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. Demands for Grants are voted by the Lok Sabha, while the Rajya Sabha can discuss them; charged expenditure is discussed but not voted upon.
accepted.tq: Separate voting power over demands from the power to discuss charged expenditure.
accepted.sec: Budget - Annual Financial Statement, Arts. 112-117, guillotine, cut motions, vote on account

accepted.s: In parliamentary financial procedure, the guillotine refers to
o: putting all outstanding demands to vote without discussion on the last day
the automatic rejection of all demands for grants
the President's power to withhold assent to a Money Bill
the referral of a financial Bill to a Joint Parliamentary Committee
accepted.x: On the last day fixed for the discussion of demands, all outstanding demands are put to vote without further discussion. This procedure is called the guillotine.
accepted.tq: Recognise the procedural meaning of a specialised parliamentary term.
accepted.sec: Budget - Annual Financial Statement, Arts. 112-117, guillotine, cut motions, vote on account

accepted.s:
Match the following types of cut motions with their purposes:

List-I (Cut motion)
A. Policy cut
B. Economy cut
C. Token cut

List-II (Purpose or amount)
1. Reduction by a specified amount to effect economy
2. Reduction of the demand to Re 1 to express disapproval of policy
3. Reduction by Rs 100 to ventilate a specific grievance

Select the correct answer using the code given below:
accepted.x: A policy cut reduces the demand to Re 1, an economy cut reduces it by a specified amount, and a token cut reduces it by Rs 100 to raise a specific grievance.
accepted.tq: Start from the distinctive numerical values—Re 1 and Rs 100—and then identify the remaining pair.
accepted.sec: Budget - Annual Financial Statement, Arts. 112-117, guillotine, cut motions, vote on account

accepted.s: A cut motion reducing a demand for grant to Re 1 signifies
o: a specific grievance against an individual minister
rejection of the entire Annual Financial Statement
disapproval of the policy underlying the demand
a demand for economy in expenditure
accepted.x: A policy cut motion proposes reducing the demand to Re 1 and expresses disapproval of the policy underlying the demand.
accepted.tq: Link the exact reduction amount with the purpose of the cut motion.
accepted.sec: Budget - Annual Financial Statement, Arts. 112-117, guillotine, cut motions, vote on account

accepted.s: Which of the following correctly describes a Vote on Account?
o: A vote by the Rajya Sabha on Demands for Grants
An advance grant for a part of the year until the Budget is passed
A permanent appropriation for the whole financial year
A grant available only for defence expenditure
accepted.x: A Vote on Account is an advance grant, usually for two months, to meet expenditure until the Budget is passed. It is provided under Article 116.
accepted.tq: Use the duration-and-purpose test to distinguish temporary authorisation from an annual appropriation.
accepted.sec: Budget - Annual Financial Statement, Arts. 112-117, guillotine, cut motions, vote on account

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements about a Vote on Account:
1. It is provided under Article 116.
2. It is usually granted for two months.
3. It becomes unnecessary in election years because the Budget is presented on 1 February.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: A Vote on Account is covered by Article 116 and is usually granted for two months. It continues to be used in election years; the change to a 1 February Budget date has not made it ineffectual.
accepted.tq: Spot the false causal conclusion in statement 3 while retaining the article and duration facts.
accepted.sec: Budget - Annual Financial Statement, Arts. 112-117, guillotine, cut motions, vote on account

accepted.s: The second batch of Supplementary Demands for Grants for 2025–26 included an Economic Stabilisation Fund of
accepted.x: The second batch of Supplementary Demands for Grants for 2025–26 included an Economic Stabilisation Fund of Rs 1 lakh crore.
accepted.tq: Retain the exact current-affairs figure and distinguish lakh crore from smaller crore amounts.
accepted.sec: Budget - Annual Financial Statement, Arts. 112-117, guillotine, cut motions, vote on account

accepted.s:
Arrange the following events in chronological order:
A. Formation of Andhra State
B. Introduction of the Andhra State Bill in Parliament
C. Assent to the Andhra State Bill
D. Presentation of the first Union Budget of independent India
accepted.x: The first Union Budget was presented on 26 November 1947, the Andhra State Bill was introduced on 10 August 1953, assent was given on 14 September 1953, and Andhra State was formed on 1 October 1953.
accepted.tq: Fix the earliest dated event first, then order the three Andhra State milestones.
accepted.sec: Universal angles

accepted.s: The Andhra State Bill was introduced in Parliament on
accepted.x: The Andhra State Bill was introduced in Parliament on 10 August 1953.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the introduction date from the assent date and the date of State formation.
accepted.sec: Universal angles

accepted.s: Which one of the following sequences correctly represents the dates connected with the Andhra State Bill and the formation of Andhra State?
o: Introduction—10 August 1953; assent—14 September 1953; formation—1 October 1953
Introduction—14 September 1953; assent—10 August 1953; formation—1 October 1953
Introduction—10 August 1953; assent—1 October 1953; formation—14 September 1953
Introduction—1 October 1953; assent—14 September 1953; formation—10 August 1953
accepted.x: The Bill was introduced on 10 August 1953, received assent on 14 September 1953, and Andhra State was formed on 1 October 1953.
accepted.tq: Order the legislative process by introduction, assent and commencement rather than by memorising isolated dates.
accepted.sec: Universal angles

accepted.s: The Andhra Pradesh Legislative Council, in relation to a Money Bill, can
o: refer it to a joint sitting within fourteen days
amend it finally within fourteen days
accepted.x: The Andhra Pradesh Legislative Council can only make recommendations on a Money Bill within fourteen days. It cannot reject or amend the Bill finally.
accepted.tq: Apply the special limitation on the Upper House of a State Legislature to a Money Bill.
accepted.sec: Universal angles

accepted.s: Under Article 200, the Governor may exercise which of the following options in relation to a Bill?
o: Refer every Bill directly to the Supreme Court
Return every Bill, including a Money Bill, for reconsideration
Dissolve the Legislative Assembly whenever a Bill is rejected
Assent, withhold assent, return a non-Money Bill, or reserve it for the President
accepted.x: The Governor's options under Article 200 include assent, withholding assent, returning a non-Money Bill for reconsideration, and reserving a Bill for the President. A Money Bill cannot be returned for reconsideration in the same manner.
accepted.tq: Use the authority-and-exception method, especially the distinction between Money Bills and non-Money Bills.
accepted.sec: Universal angles

accepted.s: Which of the following correctly distinguishes Articles 200 and 201?
o: Article 200 concerns the Governor's options on State Bills, while Article 201 concerns Bills reserved for the President
Article 200 concerns judicial review, while Article 201 concerns parliamentary privileges
Article 200 concerns Union Money Bills, while Article 201 concerns State Budgets
Both Articles exclusively regulate Constitutional Amendment Bills
accepted.x: Article 200 deals with the Governor's action on Bills passed by the State Legislature. Article 201 deals with Bills reserved for the consideration of the President.
accepted.tq: Compare the constitutional authority associated with each Article instead of confusing State and Union procedures.
accepted.sec: Universal angles

accepted.s: The five-judge Bench's advisory opinion on the Presidential Reference held that courts
o: can prescribe fixed timelines for Governors and declare deemed assent
must approve every Bill within fourteen days
cannot fix such timelines or declare deemed assent
can replace the Governor's decision with their own assent
accepted.x: The advisory opinion stated that courts cannot fix timelines for Governors in this context or declare deemed assent. It addressed the issues raised by the earlier debate on gubernatorial assent.
accepted.tq: Identify the precise legal conclusion and reject the reversed-power alternatives.
accepted.sec: Universal angles

accepted.s: The Supreme Court's five-judge Bench gave its opinion on the Presidential Reference concerning assent timelines in
accepted.x: The five-judge Bench's advisory opinion on the Presidential Reference was reported in November 2025. The Tamil Nadu Governor judgment itself was delivered in April 2025.
accepted.tq: Separate the date of the earlier Governor judgment from the later Presidential Reference opinion.
accepted.sec: Universal angles

accepted.s: The Kerala (Alteration of Name) Bill, 2026 sought to change the name of Kerala to
accepted.x: The Kerala (Alteration of Name) Bill, 2026 sought to change the name of the State to “Keralam”.
accepted.tq: Test the exact proposed name rather than the historical names of the region.
accepted.sec: Universal angles

accepted.s: The Kerala (Alteration of Name) Bill, 2026 is associated constitutionally with
accepted.x: The alteration of the name of a State is dealt with under Article 3. The Bill was passed by the Rajya Sabha during the Monsoon Session of 2026.
accepted.tq: Match the territorial-change subject with the relevant constitutional Article.
accepted.sec: Universal angles

accepted.s: During the Monsoon Session of 2026, the Rajya Sabha also passed the
accepted.x: The Rajya Sabha passed the NCDC (Amendment) Bill, 2026 during the Monsoon Session of 2026. The FCRA Bill was referred to a Joint Parliamentary Committee rather than receiving final assent in that session.
accepted.tq: Distinguish a Bill passed by the House from one merely referred to a committee.
accepted.sec: Universal angles
